Idle Resource.definition: A cloud resource (e.g., EC2, RDS) that remains active and billed while consuming under 10% CPU and low network/disk IO.
Idle Resource.financial_impact: High cumulative waste due to 24/7 billing without business utility.
Idle Resource.remediation: Stop resource outside operating hours or terminate if unneeded.

Over-provisioning.definition: A resource provisioned with capacity significantly exceeding peak demand requirements.
Over-provisioning.financial_impact: Substantial premium paid for unused RAM, vCPU, or IOPS capacity.
Over-provisioning.remediation: Right-size instance family or switch to burstable/auto-scaling instances.

Non-production Waste.definition: Dev/Test/Staging environments left running during non-working hours and weekends.
Non-production Waste.financial_impact: Up to 68% of non-prod cloud spend wasted on off-hours runtime.
Non-production Waste.remediation: Enforce automated instance scheduling (e.g., AWS Instance Scheduler).

Abnormal Storage Growth.definition: Unbounded expansion of S3 objects, EBS volumes, or log files without traffic/request increase.
Abnormal Storage Growth.financial_impact: Monotonically increasing recurring storage costs and unindexed data bloat.
Abnormal Storage Growth.remediation: Configure S3 Lifecycle policies, delete unattached EBS volumes, and trim log retention.

Cost Spike.definition: A sharp, unexplained deviation in spend compared to historical baseline behavior.
Cost Spike.financial_impact: Immediate budget overruns if left undetected.
Cost Spike.remediation: Investigate recent IAM deployment logs, scaling policies, or runaway serverless executions.

Legitimate Growth.definition: Increased cloud spend correlated directly with business growth metrics (user requests, active connections, transaction volumes).
Legitimate Growth.financial_impact: Expected cost increase supporting revenue/usage growth.
Legitimate Growth.remediation: Optimize unit cost rather than cutting infrastructure capacity.
